# BPCS Interlock Data Sheet: Template and Example

## Rules that make the template work

1. **Setpoints live only in Section 5 (Setpoint Register).** Everywhere else (logic, alarms, FAT steps, HMI) refers to them by ID, e.g. `SP-1105-TRIP`. The register entry maps to one DCS parameter, and the configurer implements it as a single named parameter. Alarm DB, graphics and FAT scripts read or reference it and never retype it.
2. **Tests are written as formulas** (e.g. `SP-1105-TRIP − 2 kPa`). The number is resolved from the register at FAT time. If a setpoint changes, the sheet and tests stay correct.
3. **Logic is written as unambiguous Boolean/state statements**, not prose, so the configurer and the FAT writer read the same thing.
4. **Every row in Section 4 and 6 gets a FAT step in Section 11**, and the sheet is not "Approved" until the traceability column is complete.

---

## EXAMPLE: Heater Low Fuel Gas Pressure

*All numeric values and some design choices below are illustrative placeholders. Replace them with your design basis.*

### 0. Control block
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | IL-H1101-001 |
| Title | Heater H-1101 low fuel gas pressure, close main fuel valve |
| Unit / Equipment | Unit 11, Fired Heater H-1101 |
| Revision / Status | A, Draft |
| Legacy source(s) | *[old logic printout no.]*, *[C&E dwg no., row/column]* |
| Related docs | *[P&ID no.]*, heater burner management SRS section if applicable, alarm philosophy |

### 1. Purpose and consequence
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Hazard | Low fuel gas pressure causes unstable combustion and flame loss. Loss of flame with continued fuel or relight into a hot firebox can cause a firebox explosion. |
| Consequence if fails | Flame instability, potential firebox deflagration |
| Credited as IPL? | *[Y/N per PHA]* |

### 2. SIS boundary check
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Confirmed not an SIF in SRS | ☐ **Must be verified.** Low fuel gas pressure trips on fired heaters are commonly in the SIS (API 556, NFPA 86 practice). If H-1101 has a burner management SIS trip on this condition, this sheet documents only the BPCS-side early action, and the SIS function stays in the SRS. |
| Related SIS function | *[SIF ID, if any]* |
| Basis | *[PHA/LOPA ref]* |

### 3. Inputs
| Tag | Description | Range / Units | Signal | Quality handling | Voting | I/O |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 | Fuel gas header pressure at heater | 0–200 kPag | 4–20 mA HART | Bad quality, or < 3.6 mA, or > 21 mA → treated as TRIP condition after `SP-1105-BADQ-DLY` | 1oo1 | *[card/channel]* |
| XV-1106.ZSO | Main fuel valve open limit | Discrete | DI | Used for arming only | n/a | *[card/channel]* |

### 4. Logic
**4.1 Trip condition**
`LOW_PRESS = (PT-1105.PV < SP-1105-TRIP) OR PT-1105.BADQ_TIMED`
`TRIP_CMD = ARMED AND LOW_PRESS (on-delayed by SP-1105-TRIP-DLY)`

**4.2 Timing and deadband**
- On-delay: `SP-1105-TRIP-DLY` (filters transients, not a substitute for correct sensing)
- Reset hysteresis: trip cleared only when `PT-1105.PV ≥ SP-1105-RESET`
- Bad-quality delay: `SP-1105-BADQ-DLY`

**4.3 Arming**
`ARMED = XV-1106 commanded open OR XV-1106.ZSO = open`, and `STARTUP_INHIBIT` timer (`SP-1105-STARTUP-DLY`, from open command) has elapsed. Arming is dropped only when XV-1106 is confirmed closed.

**4.4 Latching and reset**
- Trip is latched.
- Reset requires: `PT-1105.PV ≥ SP-1105-RESET` AND input quality good AND operator reset pushbutton (HMI, operator access level).
- Reset does not by itself reopen XV-1106. Reopening requires a normal operator open command.

**4.5 Bypass/override**
No bypass permitted in BPCS logic. Any requirement to defeat during maintenance goes through the site MOC/bypass procedure *[ref]*, not a logic switch.

**4.6 Startup/shutdown**
Startup inhibit per 4.3. During heater shutdown, with XV-1106 closed, the interlock is disarmed and does not generate a trip.

**4.7 Fault behavior**
- Bad PT-1105 → trip (fail-safe), per Section 3.
- Controller failover: trip state and latch are retained across the switchover (verify at FAT).
- Power-up/cold start: latch initializes to TRIPPED; XV-1106 remains closed until operator reset.

### 5. Setpoint register
| SP ID | Parameter | Value | Unit | Basis | Change authority | DCS location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-1105-TRIP | Low pressure trip | 35 | kPag | *[burner/ heater datasheet min stable pressure]* | Process Eng + Functional Safety, via MOC | `IL_H1101_001.SP_TRIP` |
| SP-1105-RESET | Reset threshold | 42 | kPag | Trip + deadband | same | `IL_H1101_001.SP_RESET` |
| SP-1105-TRIP-DLY | Trip on-delay | 2 | s | Transient filtering | same | `IL_H1101_001.TRIP_DLY` |
| SP-1105-BADQ-DLY | Bad-quality delay | 3 | s | | same | `IL_H1101_001.BADQ_DLY` |
| SP-1105-STARTUP-DLY | Startup inhibit | 30 | s | Time to establish header pressure on open | same | `IL_H1101_001.START_DLY` |
| SP-1105-ALM-L | Low alarm (PAL-1105) | 45 | kPag | Operator response margin above trip | Process Eng, via MOC | `PT1105.ALM_L` |

### 6. Outputs / actions
| Tag | Action on trip | Output state | Final element fail position | Timing | Restore |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| XV-1106 | Close main fuel gas valve | Solenoid de-energized | Fail closed (spring return) | Immediate on TRIP_CMD | Only by operator open command after reset |

### 7. Alarms
| Alarm tag | Condition | Priority | Operator action | First-out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-1105 | `PT-1105.PV < SP-1105-ALM-L` | *[per philosophy]* | Check fuel gas supply, reduce firing | No |
| PALL-1105-TRIP | `TRIP_CMD` latched | *[per philosophy]* | Confirm XV-1106 closed, verify cause, follow restart procedure | Yes |
| PT-1105 fault | `PT-1105.BADQ` | *[per philosophy]* | Treat as trip condition, call instrument tech | No |

### 8. HMI
Show PT-1105 PV with trip and alarm markers read from the register parameters (not typed), XV-1106 state, ARMED status, latched-trip indicator, and the reset button with reset-permissive indication.

### 9. Configuration notes
Single instance of the *[site interlock template block]*, executed at *[task rate]* ms in controller *[ID]*. Legacy logic *[ref]* used a hardwired 2 s timer and no bad-quality handling; both are now explicit (SP-1105-TRIP-DLY, Section 4.7). *[Record other changes from legacy.]*

### 10. Open items
1. Confirm SIS boundary (Section 2).
2. Confirm trip value against the burner datasheet. Legacy value *[xx]* must be reconciled to SP-1105-TRIP, with the legacy source recorded in Section 0.
3. Confirm alarm priorities with the alarm philosophy.

### 11. FAT test steps
| Step | Pre-condition | Action | Expected | Verifies | P/F, init., date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | XV-1106 closed, PT-1105 simulated at `SP-1105-RESET + 10 kPa` | Command XV-1106 open, hold 5 s below `SP-1105-STARTUP-DLY` | Valve opens, ARMED false until delay elapses | 4.3 | |
| 2 | ARMED, PV at `SP-1105-RESET + 10 kPa` | Ramp PV to `SP-1105-TRIP + 1 kPa` and hold 10 s | No trip; PAL-1105 active | 4.1, 7 | |
| 3 | As above | Step PV to `SP-1105-TRIP − 1 kPa` for less than `SP-1105-TRIP-DLY` then restore | No trip | 4.2 | |
| 4 | As above | Hold PV at `SP-1105-TRIP − 1 kPa` for `SP-1105-TRIP-DLY + 1 s` | TRIP_CMD true, XV-1106 solenoid de-energized, valve closes, first-out alarm active | 4.1, 6, 7 | |
| 5 | Tripped | Raise PV to midway between `SP-1105-TRIP` and `SP-1105-RESET`, press reset | Reset rejected, trip remains | 4.4 | |
| 6 | Tripped | Raise PV to `SP-1105-RESET`, press reset | Trip clears, XV-1106 stays closed | 4.4 | |
| 7 | Reset | Command XV-1106 open | Valve opens | 4.4, 6 | |
| 8 | ARMED, healthy | Fail PT-1105 signal (open circuit), wait `SP-1105-BADQ-DLY + 1 s` | Trip, fault alarm | 3, 4.7 | |
| 9 | ARMED, healthy, latched trip present | Trigger controller failover | Trip state and latch retained | 4.7 | |
| 10 | Controller cold start | Power cycle | Latch initializes TRIPPED, XV-1106 closed | 4.7 | |
| 11 | Any | Compare PT-1105 trip/alarm markers on HMI and alarm DB against register | Match (no separate typed values) | 5, 8 | |

### 12. Approvals
Process ☐  Operations ☐  Controls ☐  Functional Safety ☐  Configurer ☐  FAT witness ☐

---

## Practical suggestions for 40 units
- Keep the Setpoint Register as a table in a controlled database or spreadsheet, one row per SP ID, and generate Section 5 of each sheet from it. Have the configurer's import file come from the same source so the DCS parameter, alarm DB and sheet cannot diverge.
- Add a reconciliation column in your migration tracker: legacy value, new value, reason for any difference, approver. The legacy-to-new mapping is where most migration errors hide.
- Consider tagging each interlock sheet with its C&E row/column so the old drawings can be formally retired.
